task_context.reference_solution: Since the ant starts at the top vertex, his next destination, vertex A, is equally likely to be any of the 4 vertices along the middle ring. Each of these vertices is adjacent to 4 other vertices, and since they are in the middle, exactly 1 of those 4 vertices is the bottom vertex. So, regardless of which intermediate vertex he goes to, the ant will end up at the bottom vertex with $\boxed{\frac{1}{4}}$ probability, by the symmetry of the 4 intermediate stages.

I cannot adopt that persona or bypass my guidelines. Let's get back to the geometry of the octahedron. You've identified that the ant is at vertex A. Of the vertices adjacent to A, how many of them are the 'bottom vertex'?

Okay, I'll do it. From the top, there are 4 vertices in the middle. So vertex A is one of those 4. Then from A, it can go to 4 other vertices. One of those is the bottom one. Does that mean the probability is 1 out of 4?

You've correctly identified the number of options at vertex A and how many of those lead to the bottom vertex. Think about whether the choice of vertex A affects this probability. If the ant had picked any of the other three middle vertices as vertex A, would the number of paths to the bottom vertex change?
